name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.283.0 — Session token usage on ledger rows: build and review rows carry sessionTokens as their last key — the orchestrating session's own transcript usage during the stage (input, cacheCreate, cacheRead, output counters and turns) as a delta between sidecar creation and row write, deduplicated by message id because the transcript repeats a message's usage on every content-block line; null when the stamp or transcript is absent or the stamp moved mid-stage. lib/session-stamp.js gains sessionUsage(root) and usageDelta(); verdict.js gains --sessionTokens <json> (review profile only, refused on release, absent flag adds no key). Subagent spend is not included; the name says so. Motivated by the 2026-10-29 model-placement review: nothing measured what a seat change costs. 7.282.0 — Model placement refresh: core § Model Placement is a per-seat tier+effort table (planner fable/high, workers sonnet/medium, reviewer opus/high, disposer opus/medium, lookups haiku/low) and review independence is fresh-context, blind-to-author dispatch plus executed evidence — the different-model-family rule is retired. The reviewer and disposer seats are fixed aliases in their agent frontmatter, so a Fable session no longer reviews its own planning with Fable; /spec:fix dispatches the same seat unconditionally. Genesis design steps print a Dispatch line and the session dispatches Agent {model: fable, effort: high} instead of stopping for a manual /model switch. The question-style judge runs on the haiku alias instead of a dated snapshot id, and a new consistency test bans versioned model ids under spec/. 7.281.0 — Test expiry never cuts a span it cannot bound: expire-tests --apply checks every retired case and emptied describe before cutting (ends on its own paren, closes at its opening indent, holds no foreign case or describe); an unbounded one stays in its file under a new unscannable list with one stderr line, while bounded neighbours are still cut, and a file is deleted only when no line-start case or describe is left. The test-call scanner no longer reads a JSX </ or /> as a regex, so closing and self-closing tags in .tsx tests retire cleanly instead of eating a describe's closing brace.
